You know, it's funny you ask that, because my mom actually called me on Sunday—she usually calls on Sunday afternoons to catch up—and she asked me almost that exact same question. She was like, "Are you just feeling really sad lately?" And I really had to stop and think about it, because... well, no, I wouldn't say I feel sad. 

When I think of being sad, I think of, you know, watching a tragic movie or going through a bad breakup where you're crying into your pillow and your chest physically aches and you just feel this overwhelming sorrow. I don't feel like that at all. It's not this heavy, tearful kind of sadness. It's more like... well, it's just nothing. Like I was saying earlier about my art and the cooking, it's not that I look at my sketchpad and feel heartbroken about not using it. I just look at it and feel absolutely blank. It's like the emotion just isn't even there to be sad in the first place. 

Honestly, I almost wish I *was* sad, because at least sadness is an actual feeling, you know? At least if I were crying all day, I would feel like a normal human being who is actually reacting to something. But most of the time, I'm just sitting on my living room couch, staring at the wall, or staring at the login screen for my online class, and I'm just... flat. Just tired and completely flat. So no, I don't think "down" or "sad" is the right word for it at all, because that implies there's some sort of active emotional pain, and for me, it's just this giant, quiet void where my feelings used to be. I don't even cry. I think the last time I actually shed a tear was months ago, way before this whole exhausting phase even started. So yeah, I wouldn't say sad. Just... empty.

Guilty? Hmm... no, not really. I mean, I guess you'd think I would, right? Because I'm not working and I'm totally dropping the ball on this certificate program. Well, yeah, actually, I have. It's not something I was actively trying to do or anything, because like I said, I don't really care about much right now, let alone trying to diet or get in shape. You know, it's strange, but no, I haven't really had thoughts like that. And I say it's strange because, like I was telling you about just feeling so empty and flat and not even having the energy to eat or care about anything... you'd think that would naturally lead to wanting to just disappear or not be here anymore, right? Like, if life is just this giant void, why stick around for it? 

But I don't really have those dark, active thoughts about death or wanting to end things. It's almost like... well, to want to not be alive, or to actively wish you could disappear, requires a certain level of energy or despair. It requires you to be in so much pain that you want an escape from it. And like I said before, I'm not in pain. I'm not agonizing over my existence. I'm just... existing. Barely. 

I don't sit there on the couch and think, "I wish I were dead." I just sit there and think... nothing. I might look at the clock and realize three hours have passed while I was just staring at the pattern on my rug—which, by the way, is this really intricate Persian-style rug I got at an estate sale, and usually I love looking at all the little woven details, but lately it's just a blur of colors. But anyway, I just watch the time pass and I don't feel a strong desire to stop the clock permanently, if that makes sense. 

I'm not wishing for an end to it all. I guess I'm just waiting for this phase to pass, or waiting for something to change, even though I have no energy to actually make it change. It's just a very passive state of being. So, no, no thoughts of not wanting to be alive. Just a complete lack of feeling alive in the first place, I suppose.

Irritable? Well, right now, no. Like I said, I just don't have the energy to even care enough to get mad. But... before this whole gray period started, back before Halloween? Yes. Definitely. And it's so funny you ask that, because it was such a weird contrast to how I felt overall.

I was waking up early, I had all these ideas, I felt like I could take on the world. But at the exact same time, if anything got in my way, or if anyone questioned me, I would just snap. 

Like with my husband. We were talking about the budget, which, you know, is always a fun conversation anyway, but usually we just talk it through calmly. But he made some small comment—I don't even remember what it was, something about how much I spent on groceries or maybe it was about the house, like why I hadn't finished painting the guest room when I said I would, even though I had bought five different shades of yellow paint because I couldn't decide which one was the perfect, sunshiny, optimistic yellow... anyway. He made some tiny comment, and I just lost it. I snapped at him so hard. 

It was like this flash of pure, hot anger, just bubbling right under the surface of all that amazing, buzzing energy. It was like I was on top of the world, but if you poked me the wrong way, I'd bite your head off. It was so confusing for him, I think, because one minute I'm telling him how brilliant our future is going to be, and the next I'm glaring at him over a $20 discrepancy in the checking account. So, yeah, I was definitely short-tempered back then, even though I felt so fantastic at the same time. It's just... such a stark difference from how I am right now, where he could probably tell me we're bankrupt and I'd just blink at him.

Well, yeah, actually. It's like... it's exactly like that. On my slower days, which, let's be honest, is pretty much every day right now, it feels like my body is literally moving through wet cement. Loss? Or trauma? No... no, nothing like that. Honestly, that's part of what's so frustrating about all of this.
